message.reasoning_content: We need to determine the crime(s) based on facts. The case: illegal manufacturing and selling of invoices used for tax deduction. In Chinese criminal law, there is a specific offense: “非法制造、出售发票罪” (illegal manufacturing and selling of invoices). The description mentions “非法制造、出售非法制造的用于抵扣税款发票罪”. So the crime is illegal manufacturing and selling of invoices used for tax deduction. Possibly also “伪造发票罪” but the law lumps them. In examples, they used phrasing like "非法制造、买卖警用装备" etc. So answer should be: [罪名]非法制造、出售发票罪<eoa>. If multiple, maybe also "伪造发票罪"? The text says two categories: invoices for tax deduction and other invoices not for export tax refund. Both are illegal manufacturing and selling of invoices. So one crime: illegal manufacturing and selling of invoices (for tax deduction). Could be counted as two separate crimes: illegal manufacturing and selling of invoices for tax deduction; illegal manufacturing and selling of other invoices. But they are same type, just different categories. In examples, they list multiple crimes separated by semicolon. Here they might want two: “非法制造、出售用于抵扣税款发票罪;非法制造、出售不能用于骗取出口退税发票罪”. But likely they just want "非法制造、出售发票罪". Let's see similar example: earlier example about illegal manufacturing of police equipment: answer "非法生产、买卖警用装备". For invoice case, they used phrase "非法制造、出售非法制造的用于抵扣税款发票罪". So answer should be that phrase. Probably just one crime: "非法制造、出售发票罪". Provide as [罪名]非法制造、出售发票罪<eoa>.
